name: Medical public database research — discovery, extraction, analysis, figures
description: End-to-end medical public-data research across MedHelp-supported cohorts, surveys, registries, and ICU/EHR sources. The workflow uses `medhelp-database-api-access` as the permission-aware router for repeated bilingual source/variable discovery and existing-data extraction, then applies the application's mainstream pre-analysis, modeling, writing, and `nature-figure` skills. Literature work uses a compact evidence-first chain and expands only for a concrete retrieval gap.

quality_gate: The question maps to identifiable registry tables and linkage rules
Governance and small-cell / privacy constraints are explicit
Prior registry literature and gaps are summarized concretely
Database discovery completed at least three auditable passes using exact, bilingual semantic, and source-native expressions before source selection

task_blueprints.title: Map prior literature and discover eligible database assets
task_blueprints.description: Summarize the evidence and use medhelp-database-api-access to verify allowed sources before comparing eligible tables, files, modules, waves/cycles, and linkage assets. For every critical data concept, run at least three materially different discovery passes: exact/original-language, bilingual Chinese-English semantic expansion, and source-native structural terminology, normally at least two distinct queries per pass. Do not stop at the first hit. Record every query, source, kind, hit count, accepted/rejected candidate, and reason; deduplicate by source plus physical asset plus wave/version; then document known biases and governance constraints.

task_blueprints.title: Position the study question against existing registry evidence
task_blueprints.description: State what is established, uncertain, and why this cohort analysis adds value.

quality_gate: Design and time-zero logic are operational
Phenotypes / endpoints are definable in the chosen database
Success criteria include validity and usefulness
Every critical exposure, outcome, covariate, and time field has an auditable three-pass search trail, coding evidence, and wave/version-specific physical mapping

task_blueprints.title: Define cohort, endpoints, and phenotype rules
task_blueprints.description: Use the eligible-source map to lock the population, time zero, inclusion/exclusion, exposure/comparator, endpoint phenotypes, covariates, estimand, and sensitivity variants. Confirm feasibility against real source structures before accepting the design.

task_blueprints.title: Freeze the extraction manifest and variable dictionary
task_blueprints.description: Use medhelp-database-api-access to search every critical variable at least three times before extraction: exact/original-language terms, bilingual Chinese-English semantic variants, and source-native table/module/instrument/wave terminology, normally at least two distinct expressions per pass. Do not stop at the first hit. Record the full query audit and accepted/rejected candidates, resolve physical fields and files, verify wave/version and categorical coding, define derivations and QC checks, and freeze the deduplicated manifest only after the audit is complete.

quality_gate: Pre-analysis statistics and cohort characterization are documented before formal modeling
Analysis plan covers confounding, missingness, and relevant sensitivity analyses
Downloaded data and categorical coding trace back to the frozen multi-pass manifest and authorized database sources
Accepted estimates and plot-ready source data are separated from exploratory or rejected results

task_blueprints.title: Extract existing data and build analysis-ready tables
task_blueprints.description: Use medhelp-database-api-access with the frozen manifest to verify permissions, resolve physical files/columns, check categorical coding, preview safely, and export/download the complete authorized dataset without arbitrary final row caps. Build the cohort, harmonize variables, retain provenance, and document missingness, linkage integrity, exclusions, and manifest deviations.

task_blueprints.title: Run pre-analysis statistics and go/no-go assessment
task_blueprints.description: Extract the key exposure, core outcome, time variables, and minimal covariates, then run a focused clinical and epidemiologic pre-analysis to check prevalence or incidence support, crude and minimally adjusted effects, overlap, confounding signals, and whether the current design should continue, pause, or be revised.

task_blueprints.title: Generate the baseline table after pre-analysis sign-off
task_blueprints.description: Produce the cohort characterization and Table 1 only after the pre-analysis screen confirms that the exposure, outcome, and core covariates are analysis-ready or after the study design has been revised accordingly.

task_blueprints.title: Run primary analysis and sensitivity analyses
task_blueprints.description: Execute the prespecified models, report estimates with uncertainty and diagnostics, test missingness and model assumptions, and stress-test cohort, exposure, outcome, and covariate definitions. Clearly label exploratory analyses and preserve machine-readable estimates.

task_blueprints.title: Integrate accepted results and prepare figure source data
task_blueprints.description: Reconcile cohort flow, baseline characteristics, primary estimates, sensitivity findings, diagnostics, and limitations. Separate accepted results from rejected or exploratory outputs, map each manuscript claim to a verified result, and prepare a tidy source-data table that contains only real accepted analysis outputs for publication figures.

quality_gate: Methods match reporting guidelines applicable to the design
Artifacts respect DUA / safe harbor rules
The main figure uses one explicitly chosen Python or R backend and a written figure contract tied to one scientific conclusion
Every figure panel is generated from accepted real analysis outputs with source data, statistics, legend, and editable plus publication-ready exports

task_blueprints.title: Draft methods and results
task_blueprints.description: Draft the cohort flow, source/version and extraction provenance, definitions, statistical methods, primary and sensitivity results, diagnostics, and limitations. Map each claim to accepted evidence and follow the reporting guideline appropriate to the design.

task_blueprints.title: Create the main publication figure from accepted results
task_blueprints.description: Use nature-figure only after sections.publication.figure_backend explicitly selects Python or R; if it is missing, ask and stop. Before plotting, write the figure contract: one core conclusion, panel logic, exact accepted data fields, statistical annotations, and export plan. Use only verified outputs from registry_results_integration—never mock, synthetic, or guessed data—and use one backend exclusively. Export editable SVG, PDF, publication-ready TIFF, the exact source-data table, and a complete legend.

task_blueprints.title: Prepare submission and reproducibility checklist
task_blueprints.description: Assemble the manuscript, verified figures, source-data package, supplementary tables, reporting checklist, references, and sharable code or metadata according to the database policy and target venue.

quality_gate: Public materials omit protected details and follow registry communication rules

task_blueprints.title: Build clinical storyline for slides / summary
task_blueprints.description: Build a concise public-facing narrative covering the question, source and design, headline accepted findings, limitations, and implications while respecting registry communication constraints.

task_blueprints.title: Assemble permitted visuals and delivery assets
task_blueprints.description: Reuse the verified publication figures to assemble the permitted slide deck and web summary. Do not introduce unsupported results, protected details, or newly fabricated visuals.
